To solve this equation, we need both exponential terms to have a common base.

To do this, we write $64$ as ${8}^{2},$ and then we rewrite the right-hand side using the power rule of exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{8}^{5a-12} & =\frac{1}{{64}^{a+4}} \\ {8}^{5a-12} & =\frac{1}{{({8}^{2})}^{a+4}} \\ {8}^{5a-12} & =\frac{1}{{8}^{2(a+4)}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using a negative exponent: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{8}^{5a-12} & ={8}^{-2(a+4)}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(8)$, we equate the exponents and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5a-12 & =-2(a+4) \\ 5a-12 & =-2a-8 \\ 7a & =4 \\ a & =\frac{4}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
